key_insight: A data-free, continuous-time PINN produces cylinder vortex shedding, while pressure matching plus a hidden incompressibility constraint improves consistency across training windows.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports physics-only prediction of unsteady wakes and smoother aerodynamic loads across successive training windows.
method: Train over successive time windows without reference data or temporal discretization.
Break wake symmetry with an analytical, divergence-free initial condition.
Match junction pressure and penalize ∇·∂ₜv = 0, using the momentum equation to evaluate ∂ₜv.
evidence_signal: At Re=100, Strouhal number and mean drag agree with same-domain OpenFOAM results within 0.5%; the consistency remedy reduces lift-coefficient jumps 20-fold over five shedding periods.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported Re=100 cylinder case and five-period consistency evaluation; broader flow-regime robustness remains unestablished.
paper_title: Data-free continuous-time physics-informed neural networks for vortex shedding: a consistent pressure across time windows
